title: (Probable) Asan false positive with clang+windows due to _setmaxstdio causes a crash on startup
body:
### Tested versions

Tested on the 4.6 branch of godot (the latest commit), specifically f2fb4087ab01a500574ea4c4f5341dd44dd854f7

I've also tested a non editor build, non scu builds, a non dev build, and production builds, all with identical results

The clang version tested is `22.1.8 x86_64-w64-windows-gnu`, the latest msys2 has to offer as of writing

### System information

Windows 10 - Godot 4.6

### Issue description

Godot immediately crashes when run with asan enabled, when compiled with clang on windows specifically

### Steps to reproduce

Hiyas, so when compiling a custom Asan-enabled Godot version (tested: the 4.6 branch) with clang64 under msys2 as follows:

`scons platform=windows use_asan=true production=no lto=none dev_build=yes target=editor optimize=debug use_mingw=yes use_llvm=yes d3d12=no scu_build=yes`

Any attempt to start Godot immediately crashes with the following Asan stack trace:

```
$ ./bin/godot.windows.editor.dev.x86_64.llvm.san.exe                                                =================================================================
==233968==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: attempting to call malloc_usable_size() for pointer which is not owned: 0x01d7cfdeb720
    #0 0x7ffb98e4df0a in HeapSize (C:\Users\Jame\Desktop\projects\godot_asan\bin\libclang_rt.asan_dynamic-x86_64.dll+0x18004df0a)
    #1 0x7ffb98e2e436 in __asan::asan_malloc_usable_size(void const*, unsigned long long, unsigned long long) (C:\Users\Jame\Desktop\projects\godot_asan\bin\libclang_rt.asan_dynamic-x86_64.dll+0x18002e436)
    #2 0x7ffc51512518  (C:\WINDOWS\System32\ucrtbase.dll+0x180012518)
    #3 0x7ffc515844a2  (C:\WINDOWS\System32\ucrtbase.dll+0x1800844a2)
    #4 0x7ffc515843d2  (C:\WINDOWS\System32\ucrtbase.dll+0x1800843d2)
    #5 0x7ffc51584571  (C:\WINDOWS\System32\ucrtbase.dll+0x180084571)
    #6 0x7ff67898b0ee in FileAccessWindows::initialize() C:/Users/Jame/Desktop/projects/godot_asan/drivers/windows/file_access_windows.cpp:704:2
    #7 0x7ff6787d3e93 in OS_Windows::initialize() C:/Users/Jame/Desktop/projects/godot_asan/platform/windows/os_windows.cpp:343:2
    #8 0x7ff6788f9365 in Main::setup(char const*, int, char**, bool) C:/Users/Jame/Desktop/projects/godot_asan/main/main.cpp:1003:23
    #9 0x7ff6788e54f1 in widechar_main(int, wchar_t**) C:/Users/Jame/Desktop/projects/godot_asan/platform/windows/godot_windows.cpp:84:14
    #10 0x7ff6788e5971 in _main() C:/Users/Jame/Desktop/projects/godot_asan/platform/windows/godot_windows.cpp:126:11
    #11 0x7ff6788e5971 in main C:/Users/Jame/Desktop/projects/godot_asan/platform/windows/godot_windows.cpp:145:9
    #12 0x7ff6787d10fd in __tmainCRTStartup D:/W/B/src/mingw-w64/mingw-w64-crt/crt/crtexe.c:265:11
    #13 0x7ff6787d15d1 in ShimMainCRTStartup C:/Users/Jame/Desktop/projects/godot_asan/platform/windows/cpu_feature_validation.c:74:10
    #14 0x7ffc51a47373  (C:\WINDOWS\System32\KERNEL32.DLL+0x180017373)
    #15 0x7ffc538fcc90  (C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM32\ntdll.dll+0x18004cc90)

Address 0x01d7cfdeb720 is a wild pointer inside of access range of size 0x000000000001.
SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: bad-malloc_usable_size (C:\WINDOWS\System32\ucrtbase.dll+0x180012518)
==233968==ABORTING
```

The function called in question is:

`_setmaxstdio(8192);`

Commenting this out and recompiling allows Godot to boot sucessfully with ASAN enabled. Some brief googling shows that there is an *extremely* suspiciously related looking bug with MSVC:

https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Crash-with-ASAN-and-_setmaxstdio/1439907%20/

So this seems almost certainly a false positive and an upstream clang bug, likely with the same root cause. It does however render Godot's ASAN support slightly more annoying with clang on windows, which is why I'm filing this. Ideally it'd be nice to get a decorator to ignore the function when sanitising, so that clang's support works out of the box, at least until this gets fixed upstream 👍

This almost certainly affects all versions of Godot as the call to `_setmaxstdio` is still present, and I can test more if you want a triple check

This also affects C++ extensions which are compiled with ASAN under clang (as it picks up the same error), which makes it tricky to diagnose memory errors with Godot out of the box if you're not an MSVC user

Thanks!

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A (you have to compile godot from source and boot it, no project required)
